chunks: Muḥammad and al-Ḥasan, the two sons of ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, narrated to me in the year two hundred and seventy-nine. They said: Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-ʿAbdī of ʿAbd Qays narrated to us, from Ḍawʾ ibn ʿAlī al-ʿIjlī, from a man from the people of فارس, whom he named, who said:

I came to Surr Man Raʾā and remained at the door of Abū Muḥammad (عليه السلام). He called me without my asking permission, and when I entered and gave salām, he said to me, “O Abā so-and-so, how are you?” Then he said to me, “Sit, O so-and-so,” and then he asked me about a group of men and women from my family.

Then he said to me, “What has brought you?” I said, “A desire to be in your service.” He said, “Then remain in the house.” So I was in the house with the servants. Then I began buying necessities for them from the market, and I used to enter upon him without permission when he was in the men’s quarters.

One day I entered upon him while he was in the men’s quarters, and I heard movement in the house. So he called out to me, “Stay where you are; do not move.” I did not dare either to go out or to enter. Then a maidservant came out to me carrying something covered. Then he called me, “Enter.” So I entered, and he called the maidservant back. He said to her, “Uncover what is with you.” So she uncovered a fair boy, handsome of face, and uncovered his stomach, and there was hair growing from his upper chest to his navel, greenish, not black. Then he said, “This is your master.”

Then he ordered her, and she carried him away. I did not see him after that until Abū Muḥammad (عليه السلام) passed away. Then Ḍawʾ ibn ʿAlī said: I said to the Persian, “How many years would you estimate for him?” He said, “Two years.” Al-ʿAbdī said: I said to Ḍawʾ, “How many would you estimate?” He said, “Fourteen years.” Abū ʿAlī and Abū ʿAbd Allāh said: “And we estimate for him twenty-one years.”

key_terms.أَبِي مُحَمَّدٍ: Abū Muḥammad al-Ḥasan al-ʿAskarī (عليه السلام), the eleventh Imam
key_terms.السِّنِينَ: years, referring here to estimating the boy’s age
key_terms.الْحَوَائِجَ: needed provisions or necessities purchased from the market
key_terms.خِدْمَتِكَ: service to the Imam and attendance upon his household
key_terms.سُرَّ مَنْ رَأَى: Samarra, the city where the event is said to have taken place
key_terms.صَاحِبُكُمْ: your master; a designation of authority and leadership
key_terms.غُلَامٍ: a young boy revealed in the report

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith from al-Kāfī describe a witness seeing the son of Imām al-Ḥasan al-ʿAskarī (عليه السلام)?
ai.summary: This narration describes a Persian man’s service in the household of Abū Muḥammad al-Ḥasan al-ʿAskarī (عليه السلام) and his reported encounter with a concealed young boy whom the Imam identifies as “your master.” In Shia tradition, the report is significant as a narrative witness to the birth and hidden identity of the awaited Imam, presented through direct observation and transmitted through an isnad.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Muhammad said, ‘Muhammad and Al Hassan, the two sons of Ali Bin Ibrahim narrated to me in the year two hundred and seventy nine, saying, ‘Muhammad Bin Ali Bin Abdul Rahman Al Abady narrated to us from Abd Qays, from Zou Bin Ali Al Ijaly, from a man from the peope of Persia he named, saying,

‘I came to Surmanrayy (Samarrah) and I necessitated the door of Abu Muhammad<sup>asws</sup> (11<sup>th</sup> Imam<sup>asws</sup>). So he<sup>asws</sup> called me over without my seeking permission. So when I entered and greeted, he<sup>asws</sup> said to me, ‘O Abu so and so! How are you?’ Then he<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘Be seated, O so and so!’. Then he<sup>asws</sup> asked me about a group of men and women from my family members.

Then he<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘What is that which made you come?’ I said, ‘A desire to be in your<sup>asws</sup> service’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Necessitate the house (be a doorman)’. So I necessitated to be at the door, and I used to be in the house along with the servant. Then I would go to buy the necessaries for them from the market, and I used to go over to him<sup>asws</sup> from without (seeking) a permission when he<sup>asws</sup> was in the chamber for the men.

One day, I went to him<sup>asws</sup> and he<sup>asws</sup> was in the chamber for the men, and I heard movement in the house, and he<sup>asws</sup> called out: ‘Be in your place, do not depart!’ So I did not have the audacity to exit nor enter. Then a maid came out to me, and there was something covered with her. Then he<sup>asws</sup> called me: ‘Enter!’. So I entered, and he<sup>asws</sup> called the maid, so she returned, and he<sup>asws</sup> said to her: ‘Uncover from what is with you’. So she uncovered from a white boy<sup>asws</sup>, beautiful of face, and uncovered from his<sup>asws</sup> belly, and there was a growth of green hair from his chest to his<sup>asws</sup> navel, not black, and he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘This is your Master<sup>asws</sup>’.

Then he<sup>asws</sup> ordered her, so she carried him<sup>asws</sup>, and I did not see him<sup>asws</sup> after that until Abu Muhammad<sup>asws</sup> passed away. 
Zou Bin Ali said, ‘I said to the Persian, ‘How much did you serve for him<sup>asws</sup> from the years?’ He said, ‘Two years’. Al-Abdy said, ‘I said to Zou, ‘How much did you serve him<sup>asws</sup>?’ He said, ‘Fourteen years’. Abu Ali and Abu Abdullah said, ‘And we served him<sup>asws</sup> for twenty-one years’.
en.sarwar: 1. Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Ash‘ari has narrated from Mu‘alla ibn Muhammad from Ahmad ibn Muhammad who has said the following.
“When al-Zabayri was killed this letter came from abu Muhammad (a.s.).

‘Such as this is the retribution for those who lie against Allah in the matters of those who possess authority from Him. He thought that he will kill me and I will leave no children behind. How then he has experienced the power of Allah?
“ A child was born to him -that he named M.H.M.D-
in the year two hundred fifty six AH.”
